items.title: A day inside a Delhi SIR camp: Forms, confusion and long days
items.summary: Delhi is currently undergoing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, with the Election Commission extending the deadline to submit forms to August 17. Booth Level Officers are handling everything from distributing and collecting forms to digitising the data. To make the process easier, some local residents have set up small camps in their homes to help people fill out and submit their forms. We visited one such camp, where voters faced several challenges in understanding and completing the process. For many, SIR has emerged as a confusing exercise. Some also expressed fears that they could lose their citizenship because of the process. The term ‘relative’ used in the form has added to the confusion, with voters, volunteers, and even some polling officials unsure about how it should be interpreted. Abida, who is unhappy with the government and no longer votes, came to the camp after people told her that failing to fill out the form could get her expelled from Delhi. “Even if I fill out the form, will you stop the demolition?” she asked us. items.title: Chandigarh court directs Meta to remove AI-generated video of Punjab MLA Sukhpal Khaira
items.summary: A Chandigarh court has directed Meta platforms to remove from Facebook and Instagram a morphed and artificial intelligence-generated video depicting Punjab MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira in an off-shoulder women’s dress. Civil Judge (Junior Division) Kaushal Kumar Yadav passed the ad interim order on August 12 after finding that Khaira had made out a prima facie case for an injunction. “ The content uploaded is apparently defamatory, objectionable and AI generated, ” the Court said. The Court added that Khaira would suffer irreparable loss and injury if the content continued to remain accessible and circulate on public platforms. The court directed Meta, its agents and representatives to disable access to the identified video and posts uploaded on the Facebook page “Charda Punjab” and Instagram account “Chard_apunjab”. The content and identified URLs must be removed within 72 hours of Meta receiving the order, the Court directed. Khaira, who represents the Bholath constituency in the Punjab Legislative Assembly, filed the suit seeking permanent and mandatory injunctions, protection of his reputation, dignity and personality rights. According to the suit, the operators of the accounts circulated a digitally manipulated video in which Khaira’s recognisable face, beard and turbaned Sikh appearance were superimposed on an artificially generated body wearing an off-shoulder women’s dress. Khaira claimed that the video had been widely circulated and damaged his reputation globally. His counsel also highlighted objections raised over the use of his turbaned Sikh appearance. Since the identities and addresses of the account operators were unknown, Khaira impleaded them as Ashok Kumar or John Doe defendants (unknown entities). He also sought a direction to Meta to disclose their basic subscriber information Meta submitted that it was an intermediary with no personal knowledge of the content and would comply with the court’s directions. While granting the interim takedown relief, the court did not expressly allow the request for subscriber information. The matter will be heard next on September 14. Advocate Sarabjot Singh Cheema represented Khaira. Advocate Abhijeet Singh Rawaley appeared for Meta. [Read Order]

items.title: Superstition vs. Constitution: Supreme Court upholds life term of man who killed woman accused of witchcraft
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld the life sentence of a man convicted of murdering a woman over allegations that she practised witchcraft. [ Balku Oram v. State of Odisha ] A Bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and NV Anjaria held that the trial court and the Orissa High Court had correctly held the accused guilty and that his conviction and sentence deserved to be affirmed. The Court said the direct evidence on record clearly established the role of the accused and the co-accused in the killing. "The nature of the direct evidence appearing against the appellant (Balku Oram) is compelling, which clearly establishes that the appellant with the co-accused brutally murdered the deceased on the allegation of her causing death of the youngest daughter of Manobodha Naik by practicing witchcraft," the Court said. Justice PK Mishra and Justice NV Anjaria The Court also expressed concern over the continuing practice of witch-hunting and how superstitions continue to prevail over rule of law. "The malady of witch hunting still plagues sections of our society, where prejudice, superstition and irrational fear supersedes the rule of law, constitutional morality," the Court said. It noted that victims of witch-hunting are mostly women who are subjected to torture, beatings, sexual violence and social ostracisation. The Court added that blaming women for acts they had not committed reflected a deeply rooted social prejudice that sought scapegoats rather than solutions. "It often becomes an easy escape to blame a woman for the acts she did not commit, thus reflecting a deeply rooted social prejudice that often seeks scapegoats rather than solutions," the Court said. items.title: Advocates acting as insolvency professionals liable to collect, deposit GST: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that advocates acting as insolvency professionals are liable to collect Goods and Services Tax (GST) from recipients of their services and deposit it with the government under the forward charge mechanism [Kanwal Chaudhary v. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India]. A Division Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Shail Jain held that advocates providing insolvency and receivership services must obtain GST registration and comply with the requirements applicable to insolvency professionals as a class. “ An Advocate acting as an Insolvency Professional would, therefore, be governed by the ‘forward charge mechanism’, which is applicable to Insolvency Professionals, as a class, and not by the ‘reverse charge mechanism’, which is otherwise applicable to Advocates rendering legal services ,” the Court said. Justice Prathiba Singh and Justice Shail Jain Under the forward charge mechanism, the service provider adds GST to the invoice, collects it from the recipient and deposits it with the government. Under reverse charge, the recipient of the service is responsible for depositing GST. The Court clarified that its ruling applies only to services rendered by advocates in their capacity as insolvency professionals. Legal services provided by them as advocates will continue to be governed by the reverse charge mechanism. The judgment came on a petition filed by Advocate Kanwal Chaudhary, who has been registered as an insolvency professional since July 2017. In December 2018, the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) appointed Chaudhary as the interim resolution professional for Ireo Fiveriver Private Limited. A dispute subsequently arose over the payment of ₹49.04 lakh towards his fees and expenses. Chaudhary contended that being an advocate, he was not required to obtain GST registration. According to him, any GST payable on his professional fees had to be deposited by the corporate debtor under the reverse charge mechanism. In March 2021, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) rejected this position and directed him to submit GST-compliant invoices. Chaudhary challenged that decision before the High Court. The Court rejected his argument that services provided by an advocate as an insolvency professional continued to qualify as legal services. items.title: Supreme Court issues advisory against fake websites impersonating its official portal
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday warned the public against fraudulent websites impersonating its official online portal. In a public notice, the Supreme Court registry specifically highlighted one website sp-court-in.com which is currently impersonating the official website of the top court. The said the website may deceive people through phishing mechanisms and could be used to obtain sensitive personal information and confidential credentials, the notice warned. "Cybercriminals through the aforementioned link may attempt to solicit sensitive personal data and confidential credentials of the public. All stakeholders are strictly cautioned against divulging any personal / financial information, as such disclosures may facilitate the theft of data by these perpetrators," cautioned the Registry. The advisory was issued in continuation of earlier public notices dated July 16, 2025 and April 28, 2026 , warning about fake websites designed to clone the Supreme Court's official website. The registry urged people to remain vigilant and verify the authenticity of electronic communications before engaging with them. It clarified that sci.gov.in is the registered domain of the Supreme Court of India. It further advised users to verify URLs before accessing them by hovering over links before opening them. The registry also advised anyone who suspects that they may have been targeted by the phishing attempt to immediately change the passwords of their online accounts and inform their banks about any unauthorised access. Directorate of Enforcement] . Justice M Nagaprasanna responded to a submission made by ED counsel Anuparna Bordoloi that the agency was not proceeding with the investigation in the Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) or taking any precipitative action against Sammaan Capital. "Why should it remain on their heads? We will close it. They are NBFCs, when will you take action? If the ED is soft pedalling it, then there is no pedal at all," the Court said. Justice M Nagaprasanna Karnataka High Court If the ED is soft pedalling it, then there is no pedal at all. 5 FIRs were registered against Sammaan Capital between 2017 and 2021, on the basis of which the ED registered an ECIR under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. The Court noted that in 2 of these FIRs, the closure report (B-report) was accepted by the lower courts and proceedings against Sammaan Capital were closed. In the other 2 FIRs, the chargesheet filed by the police did not name the NBFC as an accused due to lack of evidence against the company. In the fifth FIR, the B-report was filed by the police after investigation in 2022. The concerned court has not yet accepted the report since 4 years, because the complainant in the said FIR had not appeared despite 10 notices being sent. Justice Nagaprasanna said that the lower court could wait for the complainant, but could not become the reason for the ED proceeding with the case. "Therefore it is virtually a nullity that the proceedings before the concerned court is now standing acceptance of a B report," the Court observed. items.title: Why four people went on hunger strike against NEET in Chennai | The News Minute
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu Assembly on August 11, passed a resolution urging the Union government to abolish NEET, citing concerns over irregularities in the examination, dependence on coaching centres and the impact on students. The resolution came as four members of the Anti-NEET Federation were completing an indefinite hunger strike in Chennai. The protest ended on August 12, after the Assembly passed the resolution, seeking not only the abolition of NEET but also greater control for states over education. In this ground report, TNM’s Nithesh Kumar speaks to members of the Anti-NEET Federation, including Anitha’s brother S Manirathinam, to understand why the movement continues to demand the complete abolition of NEET, and why the debate over the exam remains closely tied to questions of education and equality.

items.title: Bengaluru: EPFO official’s death triggers anger over road conditions
items.summary: A 32-year-old central government employee with the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) in Bengaluru was killed on Thursday, August 13, following a vehicle accident while travelling to work. Medha Akarsh from Kerala, was riding pillion with her colleague on a two-wheeler on Ananth Nagar Main Road, near Electronics City Phase II, when she met with the mishap. According to reports , a car ahead suddenly braked after a pedestrian moved towards the middle of the road. The two-wheeler rider also braked, causing the scooter to skid on a slushy, damaged stretch of road. Medha was thrown onto the road and into the path of an approaching mini goods vehicle. She was rushed to a private hospital but succumbed to her injuries. The mishap occurred around 3 km from her home, reports said. She leaves behind her husband and three-year-old son. Following the accident, residents blamed the poor condition of the road for the mishap. According to a Times of India report , residents said the stretch had remained in poor condition for years, with potholes, waterlogging and damaged road surfaces making daily commuting hazardous. Residents held a candlelight march at Ananth Nagar on Wednesday evening and also staged a road blockade, demanding immediate repairs and accountability from civic authorities. Protesters accused the Chandapura municipal council of negligence over the condition of the roads in the area. The recurrence of potholes in the stretch has been attributed partly to roads being repeatedly dug up for water and sewage pipelines, electricity cables, gas lines and optical fibre networks. Delayed or poor-quality restoration can leave repaired stretches vulnerable to further deterioration. The issue has also drawn a response from Karnataka Minister Santosh Lad. Santhosh expressed his condolences to Medha’s family while saying that the presence of a pothole did not by itself mean the entire infrastructure was poor. “I am saddened by it and my sympathies are with the family. There could definitely have been a pothole. But a pothole does not mean that the entire infrastructure is poor or that we have not spent money. We have spent a lot of money, and every year we provide the necessary justification,” he said. While the police have identified the sudden braking as the cause of mishap, residents have argued that the damaged and slippery road surface made it fatal. Following the protest, residents said the municipal council agreed to hold an urgent meeting with them

items.title: Tamil Nadu: Nine-year-old girl allegedly sexually assaulted while walking home
items.summary: A nine-year-old Class 4 student was allegedly sexually assaulted by an unidentified man while she was walking home in Denkanikottai in Tamil Nadu’s Krishnagiri district on the evening of August 12, Wednesday. The child was walking home with three other children, but the three reached their homes before her, leaving her alone when the alleged assault took place, according to police. The incident was reported around 1 am on Thursday after the child’s mother lodged a complaint with the Denkanikottai All Women Police Station (AWPS). Police have registered an FIR under Section 87 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) (kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc) and Section 5(6) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The child was taken to Krishnagiri Government Hospital for a medical examination. Police said the examination will help determine whether a sexual assault took place. A police team has also visited the scene and is collecting evidence and other information as part of the investigation. The child does not know the identity of the alleged accused, but has told police that she would be able to identify him.

items.title: Bogus law firm and fake Google notices: The murky online campaign to suppress stories on Vantara
items.summary: A suspicious entity created a fake law firm, using the identity of a noted lawyer, in an attempt to gag journalists and media outlets critical of Vantara wildlife rescue and rehabilitation centre in Gujarat’s Jamnagar, which is backed by Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries and Reliance Foundation. In another attempt, a fake google executive id was used to intimidate publishers. The murky operation, which is slowly coming to light, was carried out several months before the centre got relief from the Supreme Court. Accepting the submissions of the Special Investigation Team (SIT), the apex court had on September 15 given a clean chit to the animal rescue and rehabilitation centre. Spread over 3,000 acres within Reliance’s Jamnagar refinery complex, Vantara has been projected as one of the largest private animal care facilities in the world. While concluding that Vantara had complied with all legal requirements, especially during the acquisition of animals, the Supreme Court also told Vantara that it can pursue legal remedies against misinformation or defamation, and any such cases will be decided on merit. However, multiple journalists and newsrooms from Africa, Brazil, the Czech Republic, Germany, and India have alleged that much before the court gave such a relief to Vantara, they were targeted with fake emails, spoofed legal notices, and copyright claims aimed at suppressing their reporting that was critical of Vantara. Though it is unclear who was behind the effort to take down the stories, they went so far as to create a fake law business called ‘Aspire Law Firm’ online. The ‘About Us’ section of the firm’s website comprised the plagiarised biography of advocate Puneet Bhasin, an Indian cyber law expert. While Bhasin’s name was not mentioned, her credentials were copied to make the firm appear genuine. Bhasin told TNM she has no connection with the website or the notices sent in its name. The attempts to get articles removed happened in June and July this year, just as pressure mounted internationally with the prospect of an inspection of Vantara by the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species in Wild Flora and Fauna (CITES). The inspection was carried out in the second half of September, shortly after the SIT, led by retired SC judge J Chelameswar, submitted its report absolving the wildlife centre of allegations of animal trafficking.
